question: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Anchor: last print 2.70 (Sep 17, 2026); horizon is ~10-11 business days to the value published at the Oct 2 20:00Z resolution (FRED posts with a one-business-day lag, so most likely the Oct 1 observation). Reference class = 10-business-day changes in this exact series over the last 1-2 years: median ~0, 10-90 roughly -0.30/+0.22 over the full year but only about -0.12/+0.12 over the calm Jun-Sep 2026 stretch, so status quo (a print in the high 2.6s to low 2.7s) is the modal outcome and I keep the median at 2.71 rather than imposing drift. Skew, not level, is where the macro shows up: 10y near 5%, a Fed that just hiked with more signalled, Brent above $100 and AI-related issuance supply are widening risks, while Sep 17's risk-on session, the CR that removed the Oct 1 shutdown, low realized defaults and strong HY fund flows are the offsetting side - and at 270bp in the richest decile of history the tightening tail is compressed (2026 low is 2.60) while the widening tail is not. Two-week windows starting from tights have repeatedly produced +0.2 to +0.45 moves (Oct 2025, Feb 2026) with no comparable downside analogue, hence p75-p90 stretched to 2.79/2.93. Escaping above 3.505 needs +0.81 in 11 sessions - roughly a 1% historical frequency, nudged to 1.2% for the rates/AI-credit fragility; below 1.745 has no mechanism (all-time low since 1996 is ~2.33) so no lower escape declared. No human market prices this contract, so no crowd blend.
